headline: 250 Million Dollar Gift Will Bring Veterinary Care to Millions of Pets
meta_description: The Dave & Cheryl Duffield Foundation commits $250 million over 5 years to expand affordable veterinary care access for 50 million American pets.
summary_short: A historic $250 million philanthropic commitment aims to close America's veterinary care gap, helping millions of pet owners afford critical services for their animals.
body:
Fifty million American dogs and cats lack access to affordable veterinary care, but a landmark $250 million commitment from the Dave & Cheryl Duffield Foundation is set to change that. Announced as the "Big Bet for Pets," this five-year initiative represents one of the largest private philanthropic investments in American history dedicated to expanding nonprofit community veterinary services. The funding will support organizations working directly with families unable to afford routine, preventive, and lifesaving care for their pets—addressing what the Foundation identifies as a primarily financial barrier affecting millions of animals nationwide.

Dave Duffield, a Cornell-educated software engineer and billionaire philanthropist, built his fortune through six enterprise software companies including PeopleSoft and Workday. Along with his wife Cheryl, Duffield has already directed more than $300 million toward companion animal welfare, and founded Maddie's Fund, the largest private foundation supporting animal shelters. The new commitment pushes their total giving to companion animal causes past $500 million. "Pets are members of our families, and they need veterinary care to live long, healthy lives," Duffield stated. "For too many families, that care is not easy to find or afford."

The initiative launches with two immediate grant programs. The Duffield Boost Grants will distribute $2.5 million across 250 nonprofit veterinary clinics nationwide, providing $10,000 to each. A second program, Expanding Access Grants, establishes a $10 million pool for larger multi-year awards to established clinics ready to expand their capacity. Together, these investments signal a recognition that the veterinary care crisis affects not just animal welfare, but entire families struggling to care for their beloved companions.
quick_facts: $250 million commitment over 5 years from Dave & Cheryl Duffield Foundation
50 million American dogs and cats lack affordable veterinary care access
250 clinics to receive $10,000 grants through Duffield Boost Grants program
$10 million pool for multi-year expansion grants to established nonprofits
